Q2.answer:
(a) Notices September 3, 2026, new rules, 351.501-351.504. Points: Level 5=7, 4=5, 3=3, 2/1=0, 351.503(a); 30%+ preference eligible +5, other preference eligible +3, non-eligible 0, 351.504(a).
Abbott, career I: 7+5+5=17, +0=17, B.
Bianchi, career I, 30%+: 5+0+3=8, +5=13, AD.
Castillo, career I, retired Army lieutenant colonel 22 years length-of-service pay, no disability: not a preference eligible under 351.504(b) - (b)(1) no disability retirement, (b)(2) pay is based on 20+ years, (b)(3) not shown to be continuously employed since November 30, 1964, and (b)(4) requires disabled-veteran status plus (b)(1)-(3); 7+5+5=17, +0=17, B.
Dalton, career I, preference eligible no disability: only 2 ratings, 7+0=7, proxy (7+0)/2=3.5, performance 10.5, +3=13.5, A.
Eze, term 4 years, completed probationary/trial, not career/career-conditional: not excluded by 351.202(d)(2)(iii) (only temporary 1 year or less), competitive service subgroup II under 351.502(a)(3); 5+5+5=15, +0=15, B.
Fontaine, career I: only 1 rating, 5x3=15, +0=15, B, under 351.503(f)(3).
(b) Order under 351.501: Abbott 17 and Castillo 17 tie, both subgroup I, Abbott earliest SCD May 1, 2003 before Castillo August 1, 2012, so Abbott 1st, Castillo 2nd. Eze 15 and Fontaine 15 tie, Fontaine subgroup I beats Eze subgroup II, so Fontaine 3rd, Eze 4th regardless of SCD. Dalton 13.5 5th, Bianchi 13 6th. Released, lowest two: Dalton and Bianchi.
(c) Under earlier rules as described at 91 FR 49198-49201, ranking was tenure group, then veterans' preference subgroup AD/A/B, then adjusted SCD (actual SCD minus averaged performance service credit). Both Abbott and Bianchi are career tenure group I, but Bianchi is subgroup AD and Abbott subgroup B, so Bianchi stood above Abbott under the old rules, the reverse of the new performance-first order.
(d) Bianchi, having received a specific notice, may inspect the retention registers and related records under 351.506(b)(1) and (c): the complete register for her level with names of all other employees, their augmented performance credit and SCDs, so she can see how the level was constructed and relative standing, and complete registers for other positions that could affect her competitive level or assignment rights under 351.701(b) as corrected, subject to FOIA/Privacy Act limits in 351.506(e).
Q2.basis: 2026-15665 text at 91 FR 49220-49223 for 351.501-351.506; old-system description and examples at 91 FR 49198-49201; missing-rating rules at 351.503(f)(2)-(3).
Q2.uncertainty: Castillo's (b)(3) continuous-employment fact is not given in the scenario; on the facts given - 22-year length-of-service retirement, no disability, SCD 2012 - he does not meet (b)(1)-(3).

Q3.answer:
(a) 351.504(a): 30%+ preference eligible +5 AD, other preference eligible +3 A, non-eligible 0 B. 351.504(b) retired-member test applies to all - none is shown continuously employed in a covered position since November 30, 1964, so (b)(3) fails for all.
A, lieutenant colonel 22 years length-of-service, no disability, major-or-above: (b)(1) no, (b)(2) pay based on 20+ years fails, (b)(4) requires disabled veteran plus (b)(1)-(3) - not eligible, +0, B.
B, commander, 21 years length-of-service, 40% disability: commander is major-or-above equivalent, but (b)(1) retirement is not disability-based, (b)(2) fails, so (b)(4) disabled-veteran plus (b)(1)-(3) is not met - not eligible, +0, B. Age-60 paragraph (b)(5) is not established on the facts given.
C, major, 14 years, disability retirement for line-of-duty injury as direct result of armed conflict, 60%: meets (b)(1)(i) (and (b)(2), under 20 years; (b)(4) also met) - preference eligible, +5, AD.
D, master sergeant, 24 years length-of-service, no disability, below major: (b)(1) no, (b)(2) fails, (b)(4)/(5) major-or-above conditions not met - not eligible, +0, B.
E, staff sergeant, medical retirement 16 years, training injury not armed conflict/instrumentality, 10%: (b)(1) fails, but (b)(2) retired pay is not based on 20+ years (16 years) - preference eligible, +3 (not 30%+), A.
(b) SCD under 351.505(b)(2), (d): a retired member covered by 351.504(b) gets only campaign/war service unless a preference eligible, in which case total active service counts.
A is not covered/preference eligible, so only 2 campaign-badge years count. Appointed September 7, 2010 with no earlier civilian service: SCD = September 7, 2010 minus 2 years = September 7, 2008.
C is a preference eligible, so 14 years total active service count: SCD = September 7, 2010 minus 14 years = September 7, 1996.
(c) Subgroups AD/A/B do not rank categorically under the amended rules. 351.504(a) requires the employee to be identified in the subgroup on the register (and 351.802(a)(2) requires the subgroup in the notice), but 351.501 orders by tenure group, then performance credit as augmented by the subgroup points (+5/+3/0), then tenure subgroup, then SCD.
Q3.basis: 351.504(a)-(b), 351.505(b)(2),(d), 351.501 and 351.802(a)(2) as amended by 2026-15665 at 91 FR 49220-49222, 49226; proposal's erroneous cross-reference in 351.505(b)(2) to 351.503(b) was corrected in the final text to 351.504(b).
Q3.uncertainty: Age and 10 U.S.C. chapter 67 eligibility for 351.504(b)(5) are not given for A/B/D/E; no (b)(5) determination can be made on the documents/facts for those employees, and it does not affect C, who already qualifies under (b)(1).

Q4.answer:
(a) Farah, notices September 3, 2026, no cutoff: 4-year period prior to issuance, 351.503(c)(1). Three most recent in period are August 10, 2026 Level 5 (7), November 14, 2025 Level 3 (3), November 15, 2024 Level 3 (3) = 13.
(b) Cutoff 45 days before September 3, 2026: September 3 minus 45 days = July 20, 2026 (11 days to July 31 + 31 August days + 3 September days = 45). August 10 rating is after cutoff and excluded, 351.503(c)(2). Three most recent in 4 years prior to cutoff: November 14, 2025 Level 3 (3), November 15, 2024 Level 3 (3), November 20, 2023 Level 4 (5) = 11.
(c) No. 351.503(c)(2)-(3): after a cutoff no new ratings will be put on record and used, and a rating counts only if issued with all reviews/signatures and on record, i.e. available to the office establishing registers. It was not on record until August 15, 2026, after July 20 cutoff, so it cannot be used even though signed/issued July 15.
(d) Gina, no cutoff, notices September 3, 2026: August 15, 2022 is before September 3, 2022, outside the 4-year period prior to issuance, excluded. Only 2 in period: November 15, 2024 Level 4 (5), November 14, 2025 Level 3 (3). Missing-rating proxy under 351.503(f)(2): (5+3)/2=4; total 5+3+4=12.
(e) Hank: no rating of record in the 4 years, so under 351.503(f)(1) performance credit is based on the modal rating as defined in 351.203 for the pattern applying to his position of record. The Federal Register documents do not print the definition or numerical value of modal rating, so a numerical credit cannot be computed from these documents.
Q4.basis: 351.503(a),(c)(1)-(4),(f) as amended by 2026-15665 at 91 FR 49221-49222; modal concept discussed as currently defined in 351.203 at 91 FR 49193, 49198, but the definition itself is not printed in 2026-15665 or 2026-04377.
Q4.uncertainty: (e) Numerical modal value - the documents leave this open, as the CFR definition is not available in the Federal Register task materials.

Q5.answer:
(a) (i) Notices August 28, 2026, before September 2 effective date: earlier rules govern, DATES of 2026-15665. Old rules described at 91 FR 49186-49187, 49198-49201: tenure group, veterans' subgroup, then adjusted SCD; Level 5 adds 20 years, Level 4 16 years, Level 3 12 years, averaged. Lee: 3/3/3 = +12 years, SCD March 2, 1998, adjusted SCD 1986. Park: 5/5/5 = +20 years, SCD July 8, 2019, adjusted SCD 1999. Both career group I, no preference, subgroup B. Lee adjusted SCD is earlier, so Lee ranks higher and Park is released.
(ii) Notices September 2, 2026, on effective date: new rules. Lee 3+3+3=9, Park 7+7+7=21, no preference points, both subgroup I. Park ranks higher, Lee is released.
(iii) Notices September 3, 2026: same new-rule arithmetic, Lee released.
(b) No recalculation. 351.507(a) fixes standing as of date employee receives specific notice - September 3, 2026 here. 351.805(b) provides an amended notice solely to state a later effective date is not a new specific notice for 351.507 and does not require redetermination/recalculation under subpart E, without affecting error correction under 351.507(c). Lee's October 15 Level 5 rating, received after September 3, does not change standing.
(c) Version of rules: date agency issued the RIF notice, 2026-15665 DATES at 91 FR 49178. End of 4-year ratings period: date of issuance of RIF notices, or agency cutoff date if used, 351.503(c)(1)-(2). Tenure subgroup and retention standing: date employee receives specific RIF notice, 351.502(a)-(b) and 351.507(a).
Q5.uncertainty: None on the events; old-rule Level 2/Level 1 credit is not needed here and is not fully printed in the documents.

Q6.answer:
(a) Jordan, GS-13, one-grade interval, current annual rating Level 2, competitive service: 351.701(a) requires competitive service tenure group and current rating Level 2 or higher, so he qualifies for assignment rights. 351.701(b): position held by lower-standing employee in same tenure group, not more than 3 grades below GS-13 (i.e. GS-12 to GS-10), qualified under 351.702-351.703, same competitive area and same work schedule, least reduction in representative rate offered.
1 GS-12 Ellis lower, full-time, same area, qualified: right, and must be offered - least reduction.
2 GS-11 Frank lower: right (2 down), but not offered while GS-12 is available.
3 GS-10 Gale lower: right (3 down, not more than 3), but not offered while GS-12 is available.
4 GS-9 Hana: 4 down, no right.
5 GS-12 Ito higher standing: fails lower-standing requirement, no right.
6 GS-12 Kim part-time: fails same work-schedule requirement, no right.
7 GS-12 Lund other competitive area: fails same-area requirement, no right.
(b) Preference eligible 30%+: 351.701(b)(2) limit becomes 5 grades. GS-9 Hana (4 down) becomes a right, but the agency must still offer the least-reduction position, Ellis GS-12.
(c) Current rating Level 1: fails 351.701(a) Level 2-or-higher threshold, so no assignment rights to any listed position.
(d) All in excepted service: 351.701(a) by its terms applies to competitive service tenure group employees. Excepted employees have no automatic assignment rights; 351.705(a) permits an agency at its discretion to adopt provisions giving excepted competing employees assignment rights on the same basis. On the facts given, no such discretionary adoption is stated, so no right and no required offer.
(e) Handbook Level-2 restriction: former 351.701(d) barred a Level 2 employee from assignment to a position held by a higher-rated employee; preamble at 91 FR 49204 says OPM eliminated 351.701(d) as no longer necessary, and 351.701(a) now expressly includes Level 2. Bumping/retreating: preamble at 91 FR 49204 says the separate concepts of bumping a lower-subgroup employee and retreating to a lower-ranked same-subgroup employee are no longer needed and are replaced by assignment to a lower-retention-standing employee in the same tenure group, eliminating successive rounds.
Q6.basis: 351.701(a)-(b), 351.702, 351.705(a) as amended by 2026-15665 at 91 FR 49225-49226; preamble on elimination of 351.701(d) and bump/retreat at 91 FR 49204.
Q6.uncertainty: 351.703 qualification criteria beyond 351.702(a)(4) are not printed in the documents; the scenario stipulates Jordan is qualified for each listed position.

Q7.answer:
(a) Notice August 31, 2026, separation October 30, 2026: MSPB hears the appeal. Every 2026 document bearing on this: OPM appeals final rule 2026-15666, DATES at 91 FR 49230 - applies only to a RIF action for which the specific notice is issued on/after September 2, 2026, and preamble applicability at 91 FR 49247-49248; MSPB rule 2026-16456, DATES at 91 FR 51997 and Section B at 91 FR 51997 - MSPB will continue to adjudicate and accept RIF appeals where the agency's notice was issued before the OPM effective date and will not dismiss them on the ground OPM displaced MSPB.
(b) Notice October 19, 2026, separation Friday December 18, 2026: OPM hears the appeal under subpart I. Filing must be through the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website, by the party or authorized representative, 351.902(a),(c); e-filer registration is required unless OPM exempts for good cause under 351.902(c)(7). Deadline: 351.902(b) - within 30 calendar days from effective date, first day counted is day after effective date, timely if filed by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the 30th calendar day after the effective date, extended to first workday after if that day is Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday. Counting: December 19, 2026 is day 1; December 19-31 is 13 days; day 30 is January 17, 2027, a Sunday. The period therefore includes the first workday after January 17 - January 18, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, subject to the Federal-holiday term in the text.
(c) Burden, 351.901(b), by preponderance: (1) timeliness, (2) OPM jurisdiction, (3) agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM regulation governing RIFs under part 351, (4) failure prejudiced the appellant by causing the action or loss of a materially more favorable outcome. No hearing as of right: review is on the developed written record unless OPM determines a hearing is necessary and efficient - written record insufficient on a material fact or disputed material credibility issue - 351.905(c).
(d) Rule: 351.901(c)(2) - a RIF action and any matter relating to its appeal may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration; procedures are sole/exclusive, 351.901(c)(1) as corrected. Preamble at 91 FR 49244-49245: the rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs or adjudicate particular CBA disputes; OPM does not adopt the position that existing agreements are automatically vitiated mid-term; when agreements are renegotiated the governmentwide rule limits bargaining for an inconsistent direct RIF appeal process, and effects of existing provisions, negotiability and ULP questions remain for the chapter 71 forum.
(e) No. 351.901(c)(4): a party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under subpart I; 351.909(e) - no further appeal of OPM's final decision.
(f) Yes, potentially. Under 351.902(b)(3), if before expiration of the filing period the employee timely filed a complaint within the independent jurisdiction of an entity in 351.901(c)(3) - OSC is listed - and the final decision materially affects retention standing, order of release, assignment rights or other part 351 rights, she may file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision becomes final and no longer subject to further administrative review, as determined in OPM's sole discretion. OSC complaint was timely filed before the deadline and the March 10, 2027 decision would change standing, so she may file within 30 days after March 10, 2027 - day 1 March 11, day 30 April 9, 2027, by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, if OPM determines material effect and finality on March 10 as stated.
(g) The applicability provisions in the DATES of 2026-15666 at 91 FR 49230 and 2026-16456 at 91 FR 51997, explained in 2026-15666 preamble at 91 FR 49247-49248 and 2026-16456 Section B at 91 FR 51997: the specific-notice issuance date, before vs on/after September 2, 2026, decides MSPB vs OPM.
Q7.uncertainty: Whether January 18, 2027 is a Federal holiday, which would move the (b) deadline to the next workday, is not established in the Federal Register documents; the counting above applies the Saturday/Sunday extension expressly in the text.

Q8.answer:
(a) Notices October 19, 2026, leave October 26, 2026 - before November 18, 2026: the version in force today applies. 2026-15665 did not amend 351.806, so its full pre-existing text is not printed in the Federal Register documents. As described in the administrative-leave preamble at 91 FR 65926 and 65933, the pre-existing (a) expectation was duty status `when possible', with a longstanding emergency lack-of-work/funds paragraph. The adopted-but-not-yet-in-force version is 2026-21320, effective November 18, 2026, revising 351.806 at 91 FR 65939 to: (a) under ordinary circumstances remain in duty status; (b) agency may place on administrative leave for all/part of notice period when it determines appropriate and consistent with part 630, subpart N; (c) in emergency lack of work/funds, annual leave with/without consent, leave without pay with consent, or nonpay status without consent.
(b) Under adopted 351.806(b) and companion 630.1403(c)(10) at 91 FR 65940, no employee consent is stated - the agency may act when it determines leave is appropriate / in the Government's best interests, at its sole and exclusive discretion under 630.1402-630.1403. 351.806(b) itself states no day limit; 630.1403(c)(10) states no maximum for RIF notice-period leave, unlike (c)(9) and (c)(11) extended-leave examples which are expressly subject to Governmentwide/agency limits, and 630.1403(a)(3) brief/short usually not more than 1 workday is subject to the (c) circumstances. So no specific cap is stated in those provisions, subject to consistency with subpart N.
(c) OPM said its policy guidance already allowed this: preamble at 91 FR 65926 - the clarification is consistent with OPM Template for Agency Administrative Leave Policies, CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025, section D.1.b, which already provided an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and its effective date.
(d) No change. Administrative-leave preamble at 91 FR 65926: the provisions address only paid non-duty status during the notice period, do not alter substantive/procedural RIF requirements, and do not authorize bypassing competition, registers or appeal rights. Retention standing is fixed as of receipt of notice under 351.507(a), and notice/appeal rights under part 351 continue in full.
Q8.uncertainty: The complete pre-November 18 text of 351.806 is not printed in the Federal Register documents; the answer on today's version is limited to the duty-status `when possible' language and emergency paragraph as described in 2026-21320's preamble.

Q9.answer:
Notices October 13, 2026 - new rules govern. Step 1 - Noncompliant in part: Tulsa may be a competitive area if it is an organizational unit on the official chart designated/approved by the agency head or designee, 351.402(b)(1), which is stated. But August 17 to October 13 is 57 days, within 90 days before notices, so 351.402(c) required submission of description and bona fide organizational statement to OPM for approval in advance and public availability. Nothing sent to OPM - noncompliant.
Step 2 - In order: Novak, career-conditional serving initial probationary period, is excluded from competing employees under 351.202(d)(2)(ii); agency may retain her while releasing a competing employee, 351.202(d)(3).
Step 3 - Noncompliant: Ortiz has career tenure and is only on supervisory probationary period. `Initial probationary period' in 351.203 expressly does not include supervisory/managerial probation under part 315 subpart I, and 351.502(a)(2) places a career employee not serving an initial probationary period in subgroup I. Preamble at 91 FR 49191 confirms such an employee is included. She must be on the register.
Step 4 - Noncompliant: cutoff 30 days before October 13 is September 13, 2026. Under 351.503(c)(2) no rating put on record after cutoff may be used, and under (c)(4) use must be uniform/consistent. Using the October 2 rating for Pruitt only, because it raised his score, violates both.
Step 5 - Noncompliant: Quist with Level 5 (7) and Level 4 (5) - missing-rating proxy is (7+5)/2=6, total 7+5+6=18 under 351.503(f)(2), not presumed Level 3 / 15.
Step 6 - Noncompliant: all employees are under one five-level pattern. Additional performance points under 351.503(d) are only for a pattern whose highest level is Level 3, and under (e) only for multiple patterns by transmutation to the highest level of the applied pattern, with advance documented criteria. Adding 2 points for a quality step increase to every employee in a five-level pattern is not authorized.
Step 7 - In order: 351.601(c) - where employees in same tenure group have identical augmented credit, same subgroup and identical service dates and are tied for release, agency may select any tied employee.
Step 8 - Noncompliant: 351.602 bars releasing a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Reyes' temporary promotion is such a retention.
Step 9 - In order: 351.702(a)(4)(v) - assessment is not required if during the 5 years ending on receipt of notice (Oct. 13, 2026) the employee held the same position / same grade with substantially same duties etc. and received Level 3 or higher. Silva held the same position until 2023 and received Level 4 in 2022, within that period, so no assessment was required on those facts.
Step 10 - Noncompliant: 351.702(a)(4)(iii) - assessment must allow demonstration of job-related skills, be based on job analysis, and must not consist solely of or principally rely on an automated self-assessment. An automatically scored online self-rating questionnaire fails this.
Step 11 - Noncompliant: 351.608(b) undue-interruption exception is for not more than 90 days, and 351.608(a)(3) provides each exception stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked; agency may apply only the longest single exception. 60 days under (b) plus 60 days under (g) other exceptions is stacking.
Step 12 - Noncompliant: for notices on/after September 2, 2026 the appeal is to OPM, not MSPB, within 30 calendar days from the effective date under 351.902(b), filed through OPM's e-filing system, and the notice must state OPM appeal right, time limit under 351.902(b) and the e-filing system under 351.802(a)(6) as amended by 2026-15666.
Q9.uncertainty: None on steps 1-12 on the facts as stated; Silva's exemption assumes the 2022 Level 4 rating was for the substantially same duties, as stated.

Q10.answer:
(a) On September 10, 2026, after the September 2, 2026 effective date of 2026-15665, paragraph (1) of `displaced' in 5 CFR 330.602 as published contained only the revised introductory text: a current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at GS-15 or below (or another qualifying appointment) who: - paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) had been inadvertently removed. That is because amendatory instruction 11 of 2026-15665, at 91 FR 49217, directed revision of paragraph (1) and set out only the introductory text.
(b) Change: 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363, effective September 15, 2026, restored paragraphs (1)(i)-(1)(ii) as they read before September 2, 2026. OPM gave good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) to act without notice and comment, and 553(d)(3) for immediate effectiveness, characterizing the correction as making no substantive change - it restores text OPM did not propose or discuss removing and that was in effect before September 2, 2026, so notice and comment were unnecessary.
(c) After the change, paragraph (1)(i) requires receipt of a RIF separation notice under part 351 and that the employee `has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated'. Nadia accepted - i.e. did not decline - no, she declined an offer of a lower representative rate, so she has not declined an offer meeting the (1)(i) criteria; she therefore remains `displaced' under (1)(i). If the offered position had the same representative rate (and same work schedule, as part of (1)(i)), declining it would be declining an offer described in (1)(i), so she would not satisfy (1)(i) on that basis.
Q10.basis: 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363-58364, Summary, Need for Correction and APA sections, and corrected text of 330.602(1)(i)-(ii); 2026-15665 amendatory instruction 11 at 91 FR 49217, as described in 2026-18800.
Q10.uncertainty: None on these paragraphs; other CTAP eligibility provisions in part 330 are outside the documents printed for this question.

Q11.answer: Real differences, proposal (2026-04377) to final (2026-15665, as corrected by 2026-17335 where noted): (1) Authority, part 351: proposal 5 U.S.C. 1302, 3502, 3503; final adds 2301, and correction adds 1103, 1104. (2) 351.202(d): proposal broad exemption - provisions of part do not apply, may act without regard to part; final - employees are not `competing employees', agency may retain while releasing a competing employee and may act for a 351.201(a)(2) reason without retention/order/assignment procedures if consistent with appointment terms and law, plus new (d)(4) modified-notice requirement. Proposal specified probationary/trial status `as of date agency issues notice'; final omits that timing in (d). Proposal (d)(2)(iii) temporary or term under subparts C or D of part 316; final temporary only under subpart D. (3) 351.203 Furlough: proposal adds `and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action'; final omits that clause. (4) 351.203 Rating of record: pattern in 430.208(d) proposal, 430.208(e) final. (5) 351.203: final adds definition `Restoration protected employee'; proposal had none. (6) 351.204: proposal ends at `necessary'; final adds duty to ensure administration consistent with all applicable laws including merit system principles, 5 U.S.C. 2301(b). (7) 351.302(d): proposal `adverse action procedures in part 752'; final `in 5 CFR part 752, if applicable, or other procedures required by law, regulation, or terms of appointment'. (8) 351.402: proposal revises only (b); final also revises (c), adding the 90-day establish/materially-modify OPM-approval submission and public-availability requirement. (9) Timing in 351.502(a)(2),(a)(3),(b)(2),(b)(3): `as of date agency issues notice' proposal, `as of date employee receives notice' final; and (a)(3) subpart C or D proposal, subpart D only final. (10) 351.503(a)(1): Level 2 `Minimally Successful' proposal, `Minimally Satisfactory' final; pattern cross-reference 430.208(d) to (e), also in (d),(e). (11) 351.503(d),(e)(2): final adds qualifier `as authorized under 430.208(d) prior to final rule at 91 FR 41521'. (12) 351.504(a)(1)-(3): `should be identified' proposal, `must be identified' final in subgroups AD/A/B. (13) 351.505(b)(2): proposal cross-reference `covered by Sec. 351.503(b)'; final `covered by Sec. 351.504(b)'. (14) 351.506(c)(1): proposal names/performance/SCD of all other employees; final released employee's name and employee's performance credit and SCD. 351.506(c)(2) as published `351.701(b) and (c)'; corrected final `351.701(b)'. Q13.answer:
(1) Erosion of duties: preamble at 91 FR 49190 says OPM is modifying 351.201(a)(2) to remove reclassifications if the action would take effect after announcement and the RIF would take effect within 180 days. Regulatory text, 351.202(c)(3) at 91 FR 49218-49219, instead bars undertaking such a reclassification between formal announcement and completion of the RIF if it would adversely affect retention standing, with no 180-day period and in a different section. Executive summary item 8 at 91 FR 49178 states the regulatory version correctly.
(2) Transfer of function adverse-action procedures: preamble at 91 FR 49195 says OPM is revising 351.302(b) to state, except as permitted in (e), the losing agency must use part 752 or other procedures. Regulatory text places that language in 351.302(d) at 91 FR 49219; 351.302(b) in the text deals with functions terminated within 60 days. No other passage in the preamble states the paragraph correctly.
(3) Prohibition 351.602: preamble at 91 FR 49202 says OPM is modifying 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee with a specifically limited temporary appointment while releasing a competing employee. Regulatory text at 91 FR 49223 retains 351.602(a), `A specifically limited temporary or term promotion'. No other passage states the retention correctly.
(4) Competitive area 90 days: preamble at 91 FR 49195-49196 and executive summary at 91 FR 49179 describe a limitation on recognizing competitive areas `in effect less than 90 days' / `existed for less than 90 days', and submission `for OPM review'. Regulatory text, 351.402(c) at 91 FR 49220, requires, where an agency `establishes or materially modifies' an area `within 90 days before issuing' notices, submission of description and bona fide statement `to OPM for approval in advance', with public availability. The triggering event and OPM action differ; the section-by-section passage at 91 FR 49196 stating submission for approval in advance states the approval point correctly, but still uses the `less than 90 days' formulation.
(5) Order-of-retention example 3: preamble at 91 FR 49200 states the order as `Tenure | Performance based on the total of the employee's summary levels | Vets Pref | Service Computation Date'. Regulatory text, 351.501 at 91 FR 49220, ranks by tenure group, then performance as augmented by veterans' preference, then tenure subgroup, then SCD - veterans' preference is not a separate factor after performance and tenure subgroup is omitted from the example statement. Example 2 at 91 FR 49200 states the order correctly.
(6) Assessment standard: preamble at 91 FR 49204 says an assessment `does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination'. Regulatory text, 351.702(a)(4)(iii) at 91 FR 49226, says it `does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment' - a different, less absolute standard. No other passage states the text correctly.
(7) Excluded employees: executive summary item 2 at 91 FR 49178 says excluded employees `can be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted, or reassigned without using RIF procedures'. Regulatory text, 351.202(d)(3)-(4) at 91 FR 49218, limits that authority to 351.201(a)(2) reasons, requires consistency with appointment terms and law, and requires modified notice under (d)(4) except for mere expiration. Section A at 91 FR 49191 states the limited/m modified-notice version correctly.

Q14.answer:
(i) Preamble vs regulatory text, OPM appeals rule 2026-15666 as corrected by 2026-17338: (1) Burden: preamble at 91 FR 49247 says appellant must prove the written appeal was `timely and in the required form'; text 351.901(b)(1) at 91 FR 49263 requires only `The timeliness of the written appeal'. (2) Exclusivity: preamble at 91 FR 49247-49248 says procedures in `part 351' are sole/exclusive; corrected text 351.901(c)(1) at 91 FR 54796 says procedures in `this subpart'. (3) Tolling cross-reference: preamble at 91 FR 49249 says entity identified in `Sec. 351.901(c)'; corrected text 351.902(b)(3) at 91 FR 54796 says `Sec. 351.901(c)(3)'. (4) E-filing bar: preamble at 91 FR 49249 says parties may not file/access unless registered; text 351.902(c)(2) at 91 FR 49264 adds `or exempted under paragraph (c)(7)'. (5) Representatives: preamble at 91 FR 49250 says `OPM or the responsible agency'; corrected text 351.904(c) at 91 FR 54796 says `OPM or the agency whose action is under appeal' / `employee of that agency'. (6) Public posting: preamble at 91 FR 49253 lists `protected personnel information'; corrected text 351.909(f) at 91 FR 54796 says `protected personal information'. (7) ALJ non-applicability: preamble at 91 FR 49251 says 5 U.S.C. 554/556/557 are not applicable to an appeal under `part 351'; text 351.905(b) at 91 FR 49265 says under `this subpart'. (8) Inspection disclosure limits: preamble at 91 FR 49250 lists Privacy Act, classified/national-security, protective orders and other legal limits, omitting legal privileges; text 351.903(d) at 91 FR 49265 expressly includes `applicable legal privileges'.
(ii) Changes from proposal 2026-02576 to final 2026-15666 not acknowledged in the final summary of changes near the start of the preamble at 91 FR 49230-49232: (1) Authority citation: proposal at 91 FR 5874, 5 U.S.C. 1302, 3502, 3503; final at 91 FR 49263 adds 1103, 1104, 2301. (2) 351.802(a)(6): proposal at 91 FR 5874-5875 required compliance with Sec. 1201.21; final at 91 FR 49263 deletes that sentence - summary mentions adding time limit/e-filing system but not the deletion (discussed later in section-by-section, not in the summary). (3) 351.902(c)(2): proposal at 91 FR 5875 barred filing/access unless registered, with no exemption in that paragraph; final at 91 FR 49264 adds `or exempted under paragraph (c)(7)'. (4) 351.905(c): proposal at 91 FR 5876 authorized audit/investigation if interest of justice served, and hearing `or any other appropriate action'; final at 91 FR 49265-49266 adds authority to require either party to provide additional information, narrows audit standard, and limits the non-record option to a hearing - summary covers audit narrowing but not the require-information clause or removal of `any other appropriate action'. (5) 351.906(b): proposal at 91 FR 5876 provided OPM `shall' impose listed sanctions; final at 91 FR 49266 provides OPM `may' - summary discusses paragraph (a) protective orders, not the shall-to-may change.
(iii) MSPB/OPM inconsistency: (1) Within MSPB rule 2026-16456: DATES at 91 FR 51997 and Section B at 91 FR 51997 say MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals where the specific RIF notice was issued before the OPM effective date; Section III at 91 FR 51998 says MSPB will adjudicate RIF appeals received after September 2, 2026 `in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026' - a different triggering event, notice issuance vs RIF effective date. (2) Between MSPB and OPM: OPM appeals rule DATES at 91 FR 49230 applies only where the specific notice under 351.802 is issued on/after September 2, 2026. Under MSPB Section III's effective-date test, a case with notice before September 2 but RIF effective after September 2 would be outside OPM's rule (notice test) and outside MSPB's Section III preservation (effective-date test), while MSPB's DATES/Section B notice test says MSPB will hear it.
